version.note: The label and Victor ledger specify orchestra and organ. The precise performing edition and treatment of every written repeat are not established.

performers.note: The label names orchestra and conductor; DAHR’s Victor-ledger transcription supplies the organist. Elgar is the composer, not a performer on this record.

date.note: DAHR gives this date for issued master CVE-37282 take 3. The July 1927 date is a release-list date, not a competing session date.

place.note: Named in DAHR’s take table, not inferred from the ensemble’s home city.

label.note: The photographed label explicitly reads Orthophonic Recording: electrical, despite the archive description’s Acoustic technical note.

catalogue.note: The other side is Handel’s Largo from Xerxes. Victor’s July 1927 release list identifies the coupling.

matrixTakeSides.note: DAHR associates take 3 with issue 6648. Internet Archive’s 6648B matrix field repeats the catalogue-side number rather than identifying the master.

credits.value: George Blood, L.P.; Jordan Gold, transfer
credits.note: The item’s scanningcentre and user_transferred fields identify the digitisation facility and transfer worker.

date.note: The March 2021 upload is not treated as the transfer date.

processing.value: 78-rpm digitisation with four truncated-conical styli; engineer-selected preferred FLAC and MP3 derivative
processing.note: The item lists 3.8, 2.3, 2.8 and 3.3 mil styli but does not identify the preferred file’s stylus or equalisation. Its Acoustic technical note conflicts with the Orthophonic label and CVE electrical master prefix; the recording is identified here as electrical. No new concatenation or audio alteration was made.

digital.format: VBR MP3 derived from the Great 78 Project’s original FLAC; decoded duration rounded from cache/analysis/elgar-pomp-circumstance-1-stock-1926.txt

composition.value: Elgar’s original 1901 march is public domain in ordinary life-plus-70 jurisdictions
composition.note: Elgar died in 1934. No rights are inferred for an unidentified modern edition.

recording.value: Territorial EU public-domain basis: Victor 6648 announced for publication on 1 July 1927
recording.note: Rule 3. The Talking Machine World, June 1927, p. 157, July record bulletins, Victor list for 1 July, names 6648, Stock, Chicago Symphony Orchestra and Grand Organ. This publication evidence is independent of the December 1926 session; DAHR’s catalogue MARC estimate [1926] is not used as a precise release date. The recording’s 50-year term expired before the 2013 extension. US status is not established. The selected item’s complete metadata, original FLAC and label disclose no NC licence or separate upstream digital audio source; the University of Illinois physical-disc collection is credited by the item.
